drafts.title: Reduce harsh ride on broken pavement so bumps feel less jarring
drafts.description: When driving over broken or potholed pavement at normal urban speeds, occupants should feel fewer sharp jolts and report improved ride comfort compared with the current 5 Series.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a standardized broken-pavement route at speeds up to 45 mph, the number of perceptible harsh-shock events experienced by front-seat occupants shall be reduced by >=30% versus the current 2026 5 Series baseline, and subjective occupant comfort rating shall improve by >=1 point on a 5‑point scale in at least 80% of test runs.
assumptions: Baseline = current 2026 BMW 5 Series measured on the same standardized broken-pavement route and using the same test protocol.
Objective harsh-shock events are counted by a repeatable acceleration/jerk threshold and correlated with occupant subjective ratings.
uncertainties: Improvements may trade off with very sporty chassis tuning; customers with sport setup may perceive differences differently.
Actual field roads vary; lab-to-field transfer may differ by region.

drafts.title: Reduce distracting wind noise above 70 mph so highway driving stays calm
drafts.description: When driving at highway speeds above ~70 mph, cabin wind noise should not be distracting and should allow comfortable conversation without raising voice.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At 75 mph on a representative highway track, interior A-weighted SPL at the driver ear position shall be <=62 dB(A) and fewer than 10% of test participants shall report 'distracting wind noise' in a blinded listening survey.
assumptions: Measurement at driver ear position following a repeatable microphone placement and road/wind conditions comparable to the baseline test.
Baseline comparison is the current 2026 5 Series and subjective survey uses the same participant panel.
uncertainties: Open-window, roof-rack, or aftermarket accessories can change results and are out of test scope.
Wind-tunnel vs real-road differences may appear; tests use real-road validation.

drafts.title: Make lane-keeping assist steer smoothly in curves without abrupt corrections
drafts.description: When using lane-keeping or highway assist, steering interventions in curves should be smooth and not produce sudden, nervous corrections that surprise the driver.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: During highway curve tests at 60–75 mph (curve radii 200–800 m), lane-keeping assist must not produce abrupt steering corrections defined as >5° of steering-wheel angle change within 0.5 s; such abrupt corrections must occur in fewer than 5% of measured curve entries across a standardized curve test set.
assumptions: Test uses a repeatable set of public highway curves and a calibrated steering-angle sensor baseline from the current 2026 5 Series.
Abrupt correction metric (>5° in 0.5s) correlates with driver perception of 'nervous' behavior in prior user studies.
uncertainties: Edge cases (severe crosswinds, sudden cut-in vehicles) may still require rapid corrections and are excluded from the core metric.
Performance depends on camera/radar sensing quality and ECU tuning choices.

drafts.title: Help drivers find compatible fast chargers quickly and reliably on trips
drafts.description: When planning or navigating a long trip, the vehicle should present fast chargers that are compatible with the car and avoid recommending incompatible or unusable chargers; the system should identify compatible chargers quickly.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a 300-mile routed trip, the vehicle trip planner must propose charging stops where >=95% of proposed chargers are compatible with the vehicle's charging profile (plug/type/power), and the system must return compatible-charger search results within 2 minutes for >=90% of routed searches; recommended chargers shall require no more than a 10-minute detour versus the fastest-route baseline in >=80% of cases.
assumptions: Access to up-to-date third-party charger metadata and live availability APIs or roaming agreements.
Compatibility is defined by plug type, charging power and known network roaming status.
uncertainties: Third-party data accuracy and live availability are outside direct vehicle control.
Charger hardware failures or temporary outages can reduce real-world compatibility despite accurate data.

drafts.title: Make the charge-port indicator show charging state at a glance
drafts.description: The exterior charge-port lamp/indicator must let users see whether the car is ready, charging, or has an error without needing to open the car or look at the central screen.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: The charge-port indicator shall show at least three visually distinct states (ready, charging, fault) distinguishable by color or blink pattern from 3 meters in daylight, and in a user study 95% of participants must correctly identify the state within 5 seconds.
assumptions: Daylight visibility tests follow a repeatable lux level and viewing-angle protocol.
User study participants represent typical buyers and are naïve to the specific lamp patterns before testing.
uncertainties: Local regulations on external signaling colors or light usage may restrict some color choices; final patterns may need minor adaptation by market.
Accessory covers or snow/ice can obscure the lamp in some conditions.

drafts.title: Offer at least one variant with a real-world range of >=600 miles per fill/charge
drafts.description: Customers who request very long range should be able to choose a factory-offered 5 Series variant that delivers at least 600 miles of reproducible real-world driving on a single tank/charge under normal use.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At least one production variant shall achieve a reproducible real-world range of >=600 miles on a single tank/charge as demonstrated in a standardized long-distance mixed highway/urban test (typical driver, 2 passengers, 50% HVAC usage) with successful validation in >=90% of repeated runs.
assumptions: This requirement is met by offering an ICE or hybrid variant or other powertrain capable of such range; acceptance uses a repeatable test protocol comparable to EPA combined conditions or equivalent internal long-range test.
Customer expectation is for real-world reproducible range, not only WLTP/NEDC lab numbers.
uncertainties: Achieving this range may conflict with stricter future emissions limits in some markets and could affect powertrain choices.
Fuel availability, payload and driving style will influence real-world results; tests fix these variables.

drafts.title: Level 3 automated driving type-approval request (regulatory/homologation) — out of scope for product requirements
drafts.description: Customers request that the car obtain type approval for Level 3 automated driving in Germany.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a regulatory type-approval request (Level 3) and is handled through homologation and legal certification processes rather than as a product feature requirement.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/homologation request — compliance and type approval are handled outside product feature requirements.
